the optimal reaction conditions to achieve high degree of modification of cassava starch were at a low water content (17-19%), a high molar ratio of NaOH/AGU (1.8-2.0), and a molar ration of SMCA/AGU (between 1.1 to 1.5).

the most important parameters in controlling the DS and RE of CMS are sodium hydroxide content and SMCA content followed by water content and that the optimal conditions to obtain CMS with high DS and RE are a water content of about 20% with a molarity of sodium hydroxideto AGU of 2 and a molarity of SMCA toAGU of 1.

the optimal conditions to obtain CMS with high DS and RE were achieved at a water content between 17 and 19%, with a molar ration of sodium hydroxides to anhydroglucos unit of 1.9 and 1.1 to 1.5 molar ratio of monochloroacetic acid to anhydroglucose unit.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the DS of CMS could be controlled by the reaction variables, especially by the sodium hydroxide content.

the optimal levels for the reaction parameters were at a water content between 17-19%, sodium hydroxide between 0.8-0.9% and SMCA between 0.5-0.7% to achieve CMS with the highest DS and the highest RE.

the DS of CMS can be increased by increasing sodium hydroxide content and SMCA content, while the reaction efficiency of carboxymethyaltion can be increased by decreasing the water content and sodium hydroxide concentration.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CMS can be prepared with various DS using a statistical experimental design approach and that the properties of CMS can be modified by varying the DS.
